subject: SLA earnback plan & premium conversion options for PineLayer latency events
messages:
From: Sofia Morales <sofia@pinelayer.io>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, evan.trask@pinelayer.io
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PineLayer: recurring tail-latency incidents & next steps

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for taking this. Over the last week we've observed several tail-latency spikes on the model endpoint that powers our customer onboarding flow (peaks at ~2pm PT). The attached incident_timeline.csv shows three distinct events where p99 crossed 1.8s (normally ~300–400ms). These spikes correlate with short bursts of document ingestion.

This is starting to hit our support SLAs and is front-and-center for our upcoming renewal. We need two things:
- clarity on whether Redwood can meet a stricter latency SLO for our workload, and
- a commercial pathway: how do we handle credits, exceptions, or an upgrade if reliability remains inconsistent?

We'd prefer to avoid an immediate contract break but we need a concrete remediation and a commercial proposal that reflects the risk. Renewal is in ~30 days.

Attached: incident_timeline.csv

—Sofia
Sofia Morales
VP Engineering, PineLayer Systems
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Morales <sofia@pinelayer.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PineLayer: recurring tail-latency incidents & next steps

Hi Sofia — thank you for the timeline, and sorry for the disruption.

Quick notes and immediate asks:
- I've looped Marcus (runtime) and David (ops) to validate the telemetry and propose short-term mitigations.
- We can propose a remediation + commercial package I want to describe below; open to adjusting based on what Marcus/David find.

Commercially, one constructive path we've used is an \"earnback\" approach: Redwood issues an initial one-time credit to acknowledge the impact, and PineLayer can \"earn back\" a portion of that credit over a 60–90 day pilot if specific performance targets are met (p99 under X ms over agreed traffic profile). This aligns incentives and lets you try our Premium/Dedicated offering without immediately converting to a higher recurring cost.

Can you confirm the busiest window (local time) and whether you can provision a mirrored test workload? Marcus — can you review the attached CSV and propose an immediate mitigation (e.g., KV cache window, batching tweaks, transient sharding) plus expected p99 gains?

I'll draft a commercial amendment once we have those numbers.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, sofia@pinelayer.io
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PineLayer: recurring tail-latency incidents & next steps

Hi all — I reviewed the timeline and sampled traces. A few technical observations:
- The spikes line up with periodic ingestion events that cause short-lived KV cache churn; heavy requests then hit the full attention path.
- Our quick wins: increase prefix cache window to retain embeddings across bursts, add aggressive microbatching for the ingestion path, and apply a hot-shard placement for frequent keys.
- Expected impact (conservative): p99 down from >1.8s to ~450–650ms on the same traffic profile; p50/p90 essentially unchanged.

Proposal (technical pilot):
- 2-week controlled pilot on a dedicated pool (green environment) mirroring your peak traffic pattern; runbook attached (pilot_runbook.pdf).
- Metrics and gates: p99 < 700ms over 95% of 10-minute windows; error rate < 0.05%.
- Rollback windows and automatic fallback to shared pool if we see regressions.

If we hit the gates, we can codify the configuration as a warranty addendum and discuss a partial earnback (credit release) combined with a path to convert to Premium/Dedicated at a pre-agreed rate.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Applied Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
Attachment: pilot_runbook.pdf
From: Sofia Morales <sofia@pinelayer.io>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Trask <evan@pinelayer.io>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PineLayer: recurring tail-latency incidents & next steps

Thanks Marcus — the numbers look promising and the pilot approach is sensible. A few clarifications before we commit:
- Our renewal window is tight. To consider the earnback we need the pilot to start within seven business days and to have the commercial terms (credit amount, release schedule, and how credits affect renewal pricing) documented.
- We will want the warranty addendum to include clear SLO definitions and monitoring hooks we can both inspect.
- Legal will want to know whether the pilot requires us to move traffic or if Redwood can replay our ingestion pattern from logs. Replaying would be less risky for us.

I'll ask Evan (cc) to surface availability for next week.

—Sofia
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Morales <sofia@pinelayer.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Evan Trask <evan.trask@redwood.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PineLayer: recurring tail-latency incidents & next steps

Sofia — good to hear. Below are three commercial options (high level). I'll prepare a one-page amendment doc (attached: proposed_amendment_v1.docx) for whichever you prefer.

Option A — Remediate + Credit (no tier change):
- One-time operational credit: 20% of last quarter's monthly invoice applied up-front.
- 30-day performance window; if p99 < 700ms for 80% of windows we close with no further step.
- If gates are not met, credit remains and we discuss an upgrade path.

Option B — Earnback + Premium Trial (recommended):
- Initial credit 15% applied immediately.
- 60-day dedicated pilot (as Marcus outlined) run by Redwood in a green environment or via replay (your choice).
- 50% of the initial credit is released back (i.e., removed from your billing liability) only if we meet the agreed SLOs for 45 of the 60 days. If met, PineLayer receives the full operational benefit and has the option to convert to Premium pricing with a 10% committed discount for the first 12 months.

Option C — Immediate Dedicated Conversion + Warranty Addendum:
- Convert to Dedicated tier with an SLA addendum guaranteeing p99 < 700ms under defined traffic profile; smaller immediate credit (10%) and a 90-day warranty.
- If SLA breaches occur during warranty we provide graduated credits and a path to further remediation.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which option you want and whether Redwood should run the pilot via replay or live traffic.
2) Sign the amendment (DocuSign link in related links) so we can schedule the green pool.

I'll include David on rollout timing and any capacity reservations.

—Lauren
Attachment: proposed_amendment_v1.docx
From: Sofia Morales <sofia@pinelayer.io>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Trask <evan.trask@pinelayer.io>, legal@pinelayer.io, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PineLayer: recurring tail-latency incidents & next steps

Lauren — thanks for laying out the options; the team discussed and we want to move forward with Option B (Earnback + Premium Trial) and prefer the replay approach to avoid production changes during the pilot.

Action items from PineLayer:
- Evan will upload the ingestion logs to the shared Drive link today so your team can start the replay.
- Legal will review the amendment; please set DocuSign to include PineLayer Legal (legal@pinelayer.io).
- We need explicit SLO targets written into the amendment: p99 < 700ms (95% of 10-minute windows) and overall error rate <0.05%.

Please schedule the pilot to start on Tuesday 22 Dec (our ops team will be onshift) and confirm capacity reservations. We'll aim to finalize the amendment by Monday.

—Sofia
